name: Bright Pink
lede: Bright Pink names its own saturation on top of [[pink]], and the phrase has described vivid pinks in English prose for well over a century before it became a hex swatch.

sections.title: A modifier with a long informal life
sections.body:
As a named swatch, Bright Pink is recorded only by the xkcd 2010 crowd color survey [1]. But the plain phrase "bright pink" is far older in print: Philip Ball describes eosin, a bright pink dye made from coal-tar fluorescein, sold by BASF from 1874 [2]. David Batchelor quotes Huysmans describing a flower's bright pink as the shade of a scar in the middle of healing [3].

Its nearest named neighbor is [[hollywood-cerise|Hollywood Cerise]], only 3.0 units away and read as almost the same color [4]. [[frostbite|Frostbite]] and [[persian-rose|Persian Rose]] sit a little further out, both duller [4]. [[barbie-pink|Barbie Pink]] sits further out, duller by comparison, and the 2023 film *Barbie* used a fluorescent pink only 5.0 units from this swatch for its own branding [4].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: No painting in our 23,781-painting archive carries this exact pink covering at least one percent of its canvas, as photographed [5]. A hue this saturated is close to screen-only; Schiaparelli's 1930s shocking pink, the nearest fashion match on record, still sits 9.8 units away [6]. Our data cannot say whether any underlying pigment or dye was ever this saturated off a screen.

origin.first_recorded: 2010 as a swatch name (xkcd); the descriptive phrase is far older in print
